Q29385453.summary: Christ sits enthroned on a globe within a wreath, set against an openwork checkerboard, and reaches out to bless a model of a church offered to him by Emperor Otto the Great. Behind the small figure of the emperor stands a tall winged, haloed figure who presents him, while on the right Saint Peter holds his keys among other saints. This is the dedication image of the famous Magdeburg ivories, made for Otto's church of Saint Maurice at Magdeburg.
facts: The Met calls it one of the most famous ivory carvings to survive from the 10th century.
Magdeburg was raised to an archbishopric in 968, and the Met suggests the plaque and its companion New Testament scenes were made for the dedication in that year.
The Met notes the series was probably carved in Milan and blends Carolingian and Byzantine features.
Q29385453.notes: Met 41.100.157 (Gift of George Blumenthal, 1941). The Met mentions saints including Peter but does not name the winged figure behind Otto, so he is left unidentified here.

cur:manuscripts-egberti-woman-issue-bloo.summary: Christ, haloed and surrounded by apostles and other figures, turns as a woman crouching at his feet reaches out to touch the hem of his garment. The image survives on Commons only in a black-and-white photograph.
facts: The Codex Egberti, a Gospel lectionary made for Archbishop Egbert of Trier, is described as the oldest surviving New Testament picture cycle of the life of Christ in the Ottonian era: 52 of its 60 paintings illustrate Gospel readings in the order of the church year.
Seven of its miniatures are attributed to the anonymous 'Master of the Registrum Gregorii', who worked in Trier.
cur:manuscripts-egberti-woman-issue-bloo.notes: Only a black-and-white photograph is available on Commons.
